note: Ch4 slot 1 (b1.4 opens; hollis_told_shard honoured: Hollis had the confession at the third bell and brought Anselm, shaking; Anselm's confession is to a man he fears). c03.7a paid (the Prior: 'Two.'); c02.2a fired (she says every name every night, will go on saying all of them: Anselm's included, unsaid). Anselm named and registered; Mirren named (a mention). The wine stair (the stores key's second way down) explains the unmarked flour. T1 plants: the clerk in grey who writes and never kneels (new thread); 'the fever comes off a man through the floor if there's a stone to take it, that's how the Spire does it' (the clerk's lie, which is nearly the truth: T1/T4 edge, said by a liar, so it binds nothing). The second sliver: in Maelis's coat with the chip (she has two pieces now). Darrow's first order since the ford: Hollis's full name, 'Sit down. Sergeant.' Anselm kept in the hall with the key. anselm_suspected set. Colour: cold day, the cold in him; the hand slung.
kept_off: Oathstone/tithe; Vane's secretary (Monday: the hand on Mirren's letter); the Confessors' purpose; what Maelis will do with two pieces; Mirren's face.
next_must_know: Next: the carter brings the letter (Rae up the Steps rather than leave it in the cage), in the clerk's hand with the lock of hair; Darrow knows the hand from the direction on his brother's letters; Rae: 'I've seen that hand'. Anselm is in the hall under Darrow's eye with the stores key. Maelis has the second sliver and the chip. Hollis obeyed an order. The thin novice listens at the floor.

threads.title: The clerk in grey at the winch-house: an older man with a desk on two kegs who writes the Confessors' letters and never kneels at the dawn bell; he gave the almoner two slivers before the snow and called them the Spire's mercy for the wounded
threads.who_knows: Anselm (he saw him); Darrow, Hollis, Maelis, Wren and the Prior have it from Anselm's confession (04:s1); the reader. Marrant knows his own clerk. The clerk's name is not on the page
threads.note: 04:s1 planted: 'I never saw him kneel.' The lie he told Anselm (a stone takes the fever through the floor, as at the Spire) is the truth turned inside out

04:s1: the carrier confessed: Anselm, by the wine stair, with a trowel; two slivers came up in the satchel; the second is in Maelis's coat with the chip. The clerk's 'mercy' lie on the page. Nobody has said what the stone is
threads.who_knows: Maelis keeps the chip and now the second sliver and suspects (T1); Darrow, Hollis, Wren and the Prior have the whole carrying from Anselm's mouth (04:s1); the thin novice listens at the floor; the reader. Marrant and his clerk know what they sent
